title: JSSC cancels the Combined Graduate Level exam after leak allegations
description: The Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission's Combined Graduate Level exam, scheduled for 4 February 2024, was cancelled after allegations that general-knowledge questions had leaked. Aspirants mounted a social-media campaign demanding a new exam date, declaration of pending results, conduct of the Jharkhand police constable exam and a CBI investigation into the leak; candidates also held a protest in front of Ranchi's state library, with similar demonstrations in other districts.

title: Paper-leak allegations disrupt a JPSC preliminary exam
description: A JPSC combined civil services preliminary examination was held on 17 March 2024 across Jharkhand. At the Chatra centre, candidates alleged the question paper's seal had been broken in the principal's office before the scheduled time; about a dozen aspirants in one examination hall created a disturbance while the remaining eight halls proceeded without disruption. At the Jamtara centre, aspirants alleged the General Studies paper had been opened before it reached the examination hall. District officials rejected the claims while saying the allegations would be investigated.

title: The rescheduled JSSC-CGL exam is held — and leaks again
description: After the earlier sitting was cancelled over paper-leak charges, the JSSC held the Combined Graduate Level re-examination on 21 and 22 September 2024, with internet services suspended across the state during the exam. A CID report later found the leaks continued regardless: candidates received the answer key via WhatsApp, answers were made available by landline phone and dictated, and a photographed answer sheet was time-stamped 7:23 a.m. on 22 September, hours before the scheduled examination. About 640,000 candidates had applied for 2,025 posts; the JSSC subsequently shortlisted 2,231 candidates for document verification.

title: Mahto detained in CGL protests as the High Court halts results
description: As demonstrations over alleged JSSC-CGL irregularities continued in December 2024, police used a lathi-charge to disperse protesters and detained student leader Devendra Nath Mahto, who had contested the 2024 Lok Sabha election from Ranchi as an independent and the Silli assembly seat on a Jharkhand Loktantrik Krantikari Morcha (JLKM) ticket. On 17 December 2024 the Jharkhand High Court directed the JSSC not to declare the exam's results until further orders and ordered the registration of FIRs on the petitioners' complaints. FIRs were lodged in January 2025, a Special Investigation Team was constituted in August 2025, and the CID filed chargesheets in June and September 2025.

title: The 14th JPSC preliminary exam is held
description: The Jharkhand Public Service Commission, which had advertised 103 posts in January 2026, held the 14th combined civil services preliminary examination on 19 April 2026; more than 36,000 students appeared across two sittings. The commission's exams had previously been hit by leak scandals in 2003 and 2012.

sources.title: ThePrint — Jharkhand students are protesting 'cycle of paper leaks' CJP-style. It began with a viral answer sheet

title: Results are published — and an answer sheet goes viral
description: The JPSC published results of the 14th preliminary examination, qualifying 2,204 candidates for the mains round out of more than 36,000 who appeared. Days later, a post circulated on social media showing that a successful candidate had qualified despite answering only 48 of 100 questions in the first paper. The exam had been conducted by IT firm TSR Data Processing Private Limited (TDPL), and the viral answer sheet became the flashpoint for aspirant allegations that the recruitment process had been rigged.

title: Aspirants launch a sustained agitation in Ranchi
description: Exam aspirants launched an agitation in Ranchi over alleged irregularities in JPSC and JSSC recruitment examinations, the start of weeks of continuous protest activity. According to a protest timeline recounted by student leader Devendra Nath Mahto, the agitation was launched on 5 July, a delegation met Jharkhand's Governor on 7 July, and protesters staged an effigy-burning demonstration on 8 July. A separate report described students of the JPSC-JSSC Aspirants Justice Forum as continuously struggling since 5 July after exposing irregularities in the 14th preliminary examination.

title: A student delegation submits evidence to the Chief Minister
description: Representatives of the protesting aspirants met the Chief Minister on 20 July and submitted evidence supporting their allegations of irregularities in the examinations, according to the protest timeline recounted by student leader Devendra Nath Mahto. The meeting followed earlier appeals to the Governor and preceded the indefinite sit-in launched at the end of the month.

title: CID registers a case; the JPSC chairman resigns; arrests begin
description: Jharkhand's Criminal Investigation Department registered a case on 22 July to probe alleged malpractice in the 14th JPSC civil services examination process, and JPSC chairperson L. Khiangte resigned the same day. Also that day, the CID arrested JPSC deputy controller of examinations Shweta Kumari Gupta and TDPL directors Ramvir Singh and Abhay Kumar Tiwari. TDPL, the IT firm entrusted with conducting the examination, had previously been blacklisted by the JSSC and had been engaged by the JPSC through a nomination-based process rather than a competitive tender.

title: A torch rally in Ranchi; Mahto begins an indefinite hunger strike
description: Students held a torch rally in Ranchi on 2 August, and student leader Devendra Nath Mahto began an indefinite hunger strike at the protest site the same day. Organisers said the crowd at the Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium sit-in swelled to thousands every evening as students arrived from all 24 districts of Jharkhand, while individuals in Punjab, Delhi, Uttar Pradesh and other states sent food and money in support. Ranchi's administration refused protesters permission to erect a tent at the stadium despite monsoon rain.

title: Five more join the hunger strike; Wangchuk appeals to Mahto
description: Five additional protesters, including two women, joined Devendra Nath Mahto's hunger strike on 4 August, bringing the number of fasting aspirants to six. One of them, Rahul Kranti, on hunger strike since 4 August, was later taken away in an ambulance after his health deteriorated. On 5 August, activist Sonam Wangchuk appealed to Mahto over a live video call to protect his health; Mahto agreed to consume water and salt but maintained he would not eat until the government addressed the protesters' demands. The CID had arrested 14 people in the exam-irregularities probe as of 5 August.

title: An 11-member delegation is formed as the Assembly's monsoon session opens
description: As the Jharkhand Assembly's monsoon session opened on 6 August, protesting aspirants at Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium formed an 11-member delegation — eight students plus a journalist, a guardian and a legal expert — for talks with the state government, with the journalists and legal experts to act as mentors without participating in discussions. The protest was described as in its 13th day, counted from the 25 July launch, and 19 people had been arrested so far in the CID's investigation. A day earlier, an all-party meeting chaired by the Assembly Speaker had urged the government to open talks with the agitating students at the earliest.

title: The government agrees to cancel the 14th JPSC prelim — but not to a CBI probe
description: The Jharkhand government agreed to cancel the 14th JPSC preliminary examination along with the 2023 and 2025 backlog recruitment examinations, following talks between a ministerial panel led by Higher Education Minister Sudivya Kumar Sonu and a delegation of student protest leaders. The government also agreed to an Enforcement Directorate probe into alleged financial irregularities, a CID inquiry into criminal aspects, and a fast-track court to ensure chargesheets are filed within 90 days, but declined the demands for a CBI probe and for cancellation of the JSSC-CGL examination, citing court supervision of the latter. A march to the Assembly remained planned for 10 August.

title: Three JPSC members resign; the Governor accepts
description: Three members of the Jharkhand Public Service Commission — Ajita Bhattacharya, Anima Hansda and Jamal Ahmed — resigned on 9 August, submitting their resignation letters to Governor Santosh Kumar Gangwar, who accepted them according to an official statement. The resignations came as the CID, probing alleged irregularities including paper leaks in JPSC recruitment exams, prepared to individually question each of them on successive days that week; the CID had previously questioned former JPSC chairman L. Khiangte over four rounds and had already arrested four candidates and three alleged middlemen. The reasons for the resignations were not disclosed. The same day, Chief Minister Hemant Soren spoke at the Jharkhand Adivasi Mahotsav function, warning against misguiding the youth for political gains.

title: A shelved CID report resurfaces: most CGL questions had leaked
description: As the protests built, The Week reported on a shelved CID investigation into the September 2024 JSSC-CGL exam. The report, released in March 2025, found that about 120 of the exam's 150 questions had been leaked and that 80 per cent of the exam questions were prepared just hours before candidates were seated. After the CID submitted the report, the state government shelved it and formed a second Special Investigation Team, which dismissed the allegations. The report resurfaced during the August 2026 protests in Ranchi over corruption and demands for reforms in the tests.

title: Thousands march on the Jharkhand Assembly, breaching barricades
description: On the 17th day of the agitation, thousands of protesters marched toward the Jharkhand Legislative Assembly in Ranchi after gathering at the Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium, breaching police barricades near the old Assembly building and advancing toward the new Assembly complex, where a final barricade stood near the Jagannathpur Temple on the road to the Assembly. The JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch deployed about 500 volunteers to marshal the crowd, while authorities deployed more than 1,500 personnel from the Rapid Action Force, Indian Reserve Battalion, district police and quick-reaction teams, along with barbed-wire barricades, across a security stretch of roughly 4 km under prohibitory orders. The Assembly was in session that day.

title: Water cannon, tear gas and a lathi charge at the barricades
description: Police used water cannons when the march reached the barricade near the Jagannathpur Temple, fired multiple rounds of tear gas as protesters came within about 200 meters of the Assembly, and carried out a baton charge as the confrontation escalated; protesters faced at least three rounds of lathi-charge. Police said 14 of their own personnel were injured and characterized their action as a "mild lathi-charge," saying they would analyse CCTV footage to identify those responsible for disrupting what they described as an otherwise peaceful students' protest. Protesters reported injuries of their own: one demonstrator, Vikram Kumar of Hazaribag district, reported a head injury, and protesters said several female students were hurt. Ranchi's Deputy Commissioner and Senior Superintendent of Police defended the response as restrained, saying only mild, minimum force was used; Union Minister of State for Defence Sanjay Seth condemned the police action.

Mahto said barbed wires would not stop the marchers, and separately appealed for the protest to remain peaceful, noting it was Chief Minister Hemant Soren's birthday. title: Statewide bandh, mass ABVP detentions, and an Assembly adjourned sine die
description: The BJP called a statewide bandh from 8 a.m. to midnight on 11 August to protest the previous day's police action. The Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad marched from the old Vidhan Sabha toward the new Assembly in Ranchi; police detained more than 100 ABVP workers, including national general secretary Virendra Singh Solanki, with the RSS-linked Organiser reporting hundreds of workers arrested from different locations. Addressing the Assembly, Chief Minister Hemant Soren accused the BJP of exploiting the student agitation for political gain and announced the cancellation of the 14th JPSC preliminary examination and backlog recruitment exams and an investigation into TDPL-linked examinations; BJP legislators walked out, and after the ensuing uproar the Speaker adjourned the Assembly sine die, a day ahead of schedule. A ruling-alliance MP said 98 percent of the students' demands had been accepted.

title: Effigies burned; an ultimatum set; the opposition urges talks
description: Protesters under the JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch banner took out a torchlight procession from Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium to Albert Ekka Chowk in Ranchi on 16 August, where they burned effigies of Chief Minister Hemant Soren, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav. Manch leader Ravindra Paswan announced protesters would gherao Soren's official residence on 20 August, sought the chief minister's resignation, accused both the JMM and the Congress of playing politics with the agitation, and demanded Rahul Gandhi withdraw support from the JMM-led coalition if Soren would not listen to him. Protesters set an 18 August ultimatum for government action. The same day, Leader of the Opposition Babulal Marandi told news agency ANI the government should pay attention to the students' demands and hold talks with them without delay.

title: The government cancels the JSSC-CGL exam and every TDPL-run test
description: On the night of 17 August, after 24 days of student protest, the Jharkhand government announced the cancellation of the JSSC-CGL examination and of all examinations, declared results and selections conducted by testing agency TDPL, and ordered a comprehensive inquiry into recruitment examinations conducted from 2014 onwards. The decision followed a cabinet meeting convened by Chief Minister Hemant Soren. The government did not announce the CBI probe that had been at the centre of the agitation, relying instead on state CID and SIT investigations already under way; student leaders said the protest would continue until the CBI demand was met. The cancellation drew immediate pushback from candidates already appointed through the scrapped process — 1,932 had received appointments on 30 December 2025 — who protested the decision and indicated they would challenge it in court.

title: The hunger strike ends after 16 days
description: Student leaders Devendra Nath Mahto, Umme Habiba and Rahul Kranti ended their 16-day hunger strike in Ranchi late on 17 August, after the government's exam-cancellation announcement; state ministers Dipika Pandey Singh and Irfan Ansari attended and offered them juice to formally end the fast. Mahto thanked the state government for what he called the courage to take a significant decision, while pressing for continued reform of the examination system. Fellow student leader Ravindra Paswan said the demand for a CBI investigation remained unmet and protesters would not move from the site until it was addressed.

title: Appointed candidates open a counter-front
description: Government employees appointed through the now-cancelled JSSC-CGL recruitment — a decision affecting around 2,000 positions, including Assistant Branch Officer, Junior Secretariat Assistant and Labour Enforcement Officer posts — demonstrated outside Project Bhawan in Ranchi after the state's cancellation announcement, seeking clarity on their appointments and demanding they not be removed from service; some indicated they would pursue legal remedies. Protester Chanda Kumari said the decision had immediately put thousands of innocent candidates at risk, questioned whether cancelling an examination was the appropriate way to address alleged irregularities, and said the government had heard only one side of the dispute for the past 24 days.
